scope: Fourteenth expansion batch: 15 exercises. Six shared approximate-quantity answers accept hodo, kurai/gurai and bakari; three exercises contrast dake limitation with the explicitly named hodo/kurai/gurai alternatives; three te-bakari activity-concentration items contrast with three ta-bakari recent-completion items. This is not independent discrimination among approximate-quantity particles or complete coverage of their other uses.

sources.section: The 程 entry read hodo, particle sense 6: about/around/approximately/or so. Not the adjacent 歩度 homophone, nor a claim that an approximation imposes a hard upper or lower bound.
The kurai/gurai suffix/particle entry, sense 1: approximately/about/around/or so; explicitly also written 位. Not the separate noun for rank.

The 許り/許 particle entry read bakari: sense 2 approximate quantity, sense 3 completion after the ta form, and sense 6 always/constantly. Sense 1 also gives limitation; the batch does not deny it. The bakkari reading is outside the approximate questions' explicit uncontracted-form restriction.
The 丈 particle entry read dake, sense 1 for limitation. Not the noun take or the separate 岳/嶽 mountain entry. Its extent sense remains outside this batch's dedicated dake items.
Actual HTML Structure/About: selecting only A among possibilities and direct noun attachment. Simplified extraction initially returned only a forum discussion; the actual grammar body was inspected.
Te-form + bakari for concentration on an activity. The About section explicitly says iru often follows but is not required, supporting the te-bakari desu frames used here.

Past-form + bakari for a just-completed action; distinguishes approximate amount, limitation and completion. The actual HTML Related section also acknowledges overlap with ta tokoro, rather than claiming the constructions can never describe the same event.

Sections 1-4 distinguish recent completion, noun-based concentration, approximate time/counter quantities and te-form activity concentration. A one-week-ago meeting example in Note 1 supports recency beyond an immediate clock-time threshold. Its colloquial variants are acknowledged, not universally rejected.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original and require independent linguistic review. Dictionary senses identify valid functions and spellings, not automatic acceptability in every invented sentence.

The six approximation items explicitly request an approximate quantity and name uncontracted hodo, kurai, gurai, bakari or dake, in kana or kanji. Each accepts the same eight literal strings. Three model buttons show hodo and three show the kurai/gurai family; bakari is an accepted alternative, not an independently discriminated quantity target.

The three limitation items deliberately name only hodo, kurai, gurai or dake. This avoids rejecting a possible limitation use of bakari in an unrestricted task. The intended exclusive-limit versus estimate distinction is question-visible; do not remove either the named list or that framing.

The activity items request only te or ta forms of the supplied verbs before printed bakari desu. The same three verbs occur on both sides. Forms ending in de/da are te/ta forms too. The pleasant holiday-reading example avoids implying that every concentration use must be criticism.

The yesterday-book item protects speaker-relative recency rather than a fixed short time limit. Ta tokoro and other ways to describe completion can be natural, but are outside the printed bakari frame.

The full article inventory was screened. Quantity overlap is not exported to proportional or negative-comparison hodo, degree/minimum kurai, extent dake or every bakari construction. Those and additional uses of previously covered formal nouns still need expansion.

Bunpro's separate hodo page was inspected but its claim that hodo can never exceed a stated limit is not adopted as a rule for approximate numeric quantities. JMdict's actual approximate-quantity sense is used here.
All prior 182 exercise records remain unchanged against preservationBaseline. A shared answer set has one exercise/SRS identity, not one per particle spelling or model button.
